Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Implementation velocity: onboarding benchmark & telemetry bridge

Hi Maya —

Congrats again on signing the Dedicated contract. Next step from CS -> Implementation: we want to align on the acceptance benchmarks (latency P95, throughput targets, and stress test cadence) and the telemetry artifacts you’ll share. Proposed plan below: 

- Acceptance targets: P95 latency <= 180ms (single-request, 64-token prompt) and sustained throughput 350 rps for 30 minutes with <1% error rate
- Test windows: pre-production smoke (3x short runs) on 7/26, full ramp tests on 7/27 (capacity + tail latency)
- Artifacts we need from Fastlane: telemetry export (sample traces), request size distribution, spike scenarios, and a signed SLO acceptance email by your Ops lead
- Attachments: fastlane-onboard-loadplan-v1.xlsx (you can edit); we will produce run artifacts post-test, including run-results-YYYYMMDD.csv and telemetry-sample.json

Ben: can you confirm resource recommendations for the Dedicated pool (batching config + preferred quantization profile)?
Monica: I’ll own coordinating the test window and collecting artifacts into the onboarding Drive.

Maya — once you confirm the windows above we’ll lock the ramp script and invite your infra team to the 7/27 run Slack channel.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: fastlane-onboard-loadplan-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

Subject: Re: Implementation velocity: onboarding benchmark & telemetry bridge

Thanks, Evelyn — this looks good and doable. Quick confirmations and a couple notes:

- Targets: Fastlane agrees to P95 <= 180ms and will aim for 350 rps sustained. We do want to capture tail-latency at P99 and 99.9 for the full run.
- Test windows: 7/26 pre-prod smoke OK; confirm 7/27 full run 14:00-16:00 PDT
- Telemetry we can export: span traces (Jaeger format), sample request payloads, and a histogram of request sizes. I'll attach a small sample telemetry export (telemetry-sample-20280725.json) to this thread and update the spreadsheet.

A couple asks for Redwood:
1) Please share the exact ramp script we will execute so our SREs can simulate locally first.
2) If the Dedicated pool needs specific kernel or quantization flags, let us know so we can pre-lint images.

James (cc): please confirm Ops approval for the 7/27 two-hour window.

Cheers,
Maya Tran
Product Manager, Fastlane.ai
maya.tran@fastlane.ai

Attachments: telemetry-sample-20280725.json (JSON, 34KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation velocity: onboarding benchmark & telemetry bridge

Evelyn / Monica —

Confirmed. For the Dedicated pool we recommend the following starter config for the 350 rps target:

- Instance tier: d3.8x (8xA100-equivalent) with 4 workers behind the router
- Batching: continuous batching with 64-token max batch, target batch latency 8ms
- KV cache: Enabled with 8GB per worker; TTL 30min for in-flight sessions
- Quantization: q4f16 for the primary model; fallback q4_0 for memory-constrained runs
- Kernel flags: enable fast-attn and fused-gemm (these are defaults on the Dedicated image v1.8)

I’ll upload the ramp script (ramp-driver.sh) to the Drive and paste the run steps below before the 7/27 run. Expect ~20–30% headroom on that config; adjust to d3.12x if you hit memory pressure.

Ben
Performance Eng | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Evelyn / team —

Ops signed off on the window. We ran the full ramp per the attached script and configuration. Summary of results (high level):

- Sustained throughput: 360 rps over the 30-minute steady window (PASS)
- P95 latency: 172ms (PASS)
- P99 latency: 290ms (marginal) — we observed a small fraction of spikes during cold-cache segments
- Errors: 0.6% (PASS)

Artifacts attached: run-results-20280727.csv, a zipped subset of Jaeger traces (see Drive), and a short Ops readout (rd-support@fastlane.ai noted a transient retry loop in our client lib).

Next steps from Fastlane side:
1) We will sanitize and upload the full trace bundle to the shared Drive by EOD Mon 7/30.
2) Ops requested a follow-up on cache-warming and a recommended TTL change; can Ben propose a short config change (5–10 min) to reduce P99?

Thanks for the clear ramp script and for joining the run — good collaboration.

James Lee
Head of Operations, Fastlane.ai
james.lee@fastlane.ai
